newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL would agree to fare hike for in-bound flights.
newsitem.headline: JAL would agree to fare hike for in-bound flights.

text.p: Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) said on Wednesday that it would be prepared to raise fares for flights into Japan as part of moves to counter the impact of rising fuel costs on international airlines.
But the company has not yet decided on whether it would agree to raise fares for domestic flights and for international flights from Japan, JAL managing director Jiro Sagara said.

The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has called an emergency meeting of its 250 member airlines for mid-November to discuss joint action to offset the burden on airlines of rising fuel costs.
Sagara told a news conference that air tickets sold in Japan are already expensive compared to tickets sold abroad, hence the reluctance to raise the cost of flights out of Japan.

An IATA spokesman said on Tuesday that the body would decide on passenger fare and cargo rate increases at the talks, to be held in Geneva, or may elect to absorb the rise in fuel costs so far this year.
A spokesman for All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA), another Japanese international carrier, said earlier on Wednesday that it had not yet decided what stance to take at the November 13 meeting.
